actual_hs_list: 847130 (portable automatic data-processing machines, <10 kg — for Tactera braille notetaker, if classified as ADP)
847160 (input/output units — braille display/keyboard peripherals; alternative for Tactera)
854370 (electrical machines/apparatus with individual functions, n.e.s. — Annie braille learning device, tactile/audio teaching hardware)
902300 (instruments/apparatus for demonstration/teaching purposes — alternative for Annie as educational apparatus)
950490 / 950430 (games/educational interactive devices — only if classified as gamified learning apparatus; weak)
product_summary: Website (thinkerbelllabs.com, home + /annie + /tactera pages) shows two hardware products: (1) Annie — 'world's first self-learning braille learning device': purpose-built tactile hardware with twin large braille cells, standard 6-cell braille display, braille keyboard, built-in speakers, Wi-Fi & Bluetooth, Ethernet & USB ports, vibration motor, voice-guided lessons in 14+ languages; sold to schools/governments/NGOs, deployed in 26 Indian states and 8+ countries. (2) Tactera — 'upcoming' 32-cell refreshable braille notetaker: 32 x 8-dot braille cells, 8 Perkins keys, 32 cursor routers, 5000 mAh battery, Wi-Fi 5.0, Bluetooth 5.0, 32 GB storage, USB-A/USB-C, AI companion app. Also software/analytics platform 'Helios' (classroom progress analytics) and content/curriculum. No customs line, invoice or shipping document was found on the public site — product existence is documented, shipment-level HS corroboration is not.
comment: HS mismatch — company retained, code corrected (per Rule 3, HS mismatch never rejects). Declared 847150 (ADP processing units) and 847350 (parts/accessories of ADP of 8471) do not match the actual product line. 847150 is a bare processing-unit code and 847350 covers ADP parts — neither describes a finished assistive braille device. Annie is a self-contained tactile/audio teaching device with its own braille cells, keyboard and speakers, not an ADP unit or an ADP part: best fit is 854370 (apparatus with individual function, n.e.s.) or 902300 (apparatus for demonstration/teaching), with 854370 preferred for the electronic tactile hardware. Tactera, a 32-cell refreshable braille notetaker with storage, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth and apps, is closer to 847130 (portable ADP machine) or 847160 (input/output unit) — so 8471-family codes are only partially defensible, and only for Tactera, which the site itself labels 'upcoming / coming soon' and 'specifications subject to change', i.e. not yet a shipped product. Net: declared codes are wrong for the flagship product (Annie) and at best partial for the not-yet-launched Tactera. Industry label 'IT и электроника' is a misclassification in substance: this is assistive technology / educational hardware for the blind and visually impaired (ed-tech + accessibility devices), not general IT/electronics trading. Product lines missing from the declaration: braille learning hardware (Annie), refreshable braille display/notetaker (Tactera), and software/analytics (Helios) plus curriculum content — software and content are not classifiable under 8471 at all. No trader signs found: the site presents own-designed, own-branded, 'Made-in-India' engineered hardware with named co-founders and an in-house product ecosystem, consistent with a manufacturer role, not a reseller. All product claims are 'заявлено, не подтверждено' at HS level: no customs line, B-L or invoice was located to corroborate any specific HS-6 code, so the corrected codes above are proposed classifications from the published product specifications, not confirmed declarations.
